features.quote: the water was collected in a basin beneath the crypt
features.subtype: spring basin ('Ein Samiyeh) beneath Byzantine church crypt

date.basis: basin itself not dated; it lay beneath the crypt of the Byzantine church

features.quote: a courtyard with two storage bins built with field stones

date.basis: publication places them in the eighth-century (Iron Age) living areas above the destruction layer

notes: No plan in the note. s4f1: 'basin' with no size; coded pool with pool_def 'no' because the source puts it beneath the church crypt (not open). It could equally be read as a roofed water chamber (pit). Position: the excavated area is 'about 20 m north of Ein Samiyeh', the spring from which the basin was fed, so the basin is c. 20 m S of the excavation area (relative to other, not to the unit). s4f2: the bins lie in the excavated area, c. 20 m N of the spring (relative to other). Including them as pits (silos) is marginal: the source calls them stone-built storage bins and does not say they are sunk. No WBADB row in the packet is clearly the same place as the spring basin (E222/S1676 'Ein Samiya, 707 m S, is a cemetery). No grave or burial mentioned; no absence statement.
